prompt: Split an int array into runs of consecutive equal values. Complete the segments method so it returns a 2D array whose rows are {value, runLength}.
explanation: A run ends whenever the current element differs from the one before it, so a single pass comparing values[i] with values[i - 1] finds every boundary. Because a Java 2D array needs its row count up front, the reference solution counts the runs in a first pass and fills them in a second. The empty array is the edge case worth naming: it has zero runs, so the result is new int[0][].
hints: Walk the array once comparing values[i] with values[i - 1]; every time they differ you have started a new run.
An int[][] must be sized before you fill it, so count the runs in one pass and then build new int[runs][2] in a second pass.
Handle the empty array before the loops: with no elements there are no runs at all.
